title: Closed immersions of universally closed algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the point spaces of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Local finite type and unramifiedness mean the chart test of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] applied to the scheme properties [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism], respectively. Universally injective means injective on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. Let $g:X\to Y$ be universally closed, meaning closed on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Then $g$ is a closed immersion if and only if $g$ is unramified and universally injective. Here a closed immersion means a representable morphism whose every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 05W8 (spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-characterize-closed-immersion), equivalence of (1) and (3), with universal closedness fixed.

proof.text: Assume $g$ is a closed immersion. It is representable, and for every scheme $T\to Y$ the scheme morphism $g_T:X\times_YT\to T$ is a closed immersion, by the meaning of closed immersion in the statement. It is universally closed as a scheme morphism: for any scheme $T'\to T$, its further base change is the base change of $g$ along $T'\to Y$, hence is closed by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Apply [lem-sfb-universally-closed-unramified-radicial-criterion] to $g_T$. Thus every such $g_T$ is unramified and universally injective in the scheme sense.

source.place: Tag 05W8 (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion), forward implication by scheme tests and Tag 04XV.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Since $g$ is representable, $U=X\times_YV$ is a scheme. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], its projection $U\to X$ is representable surjective etale. The cartesian square with bottom arrow $g$ and top arrow $g_V:U\to V$ is therefore a compatible chart diagram with surjective source chart. Its top arrow is unramified by step 1, so [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] gives chartwise unramifiedness of $g$.

source.place: Tag 05W8, forward implication; scheme-test/chart comparison as in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZK (lemma-unramified-local).

proof.text: To check universal injectivity, let $Z\to Y$ be any algebraic-space map and take two point classes of $X\times_YZ$ with the same image in $|Z|$. By [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes], extend their field representatives to a common field $K$ where their $Z$-components agree. Their $X$-components then lie over the same $y:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$. They define two $K$-valued points of the scheme $X\times_{Y,y}\operatorname{Spec}K$ over its identity $K$-point. Step 1 says this scheme morphism is universally injective; the field-valued injectivity criterion stated in [def-weil-radicial-morphism] makes these points equal. The pointwise fibre-product identity [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] now makes the two representatives in $X\times_YZ$ equal over $K$, so their point classes agree. This proves injectivity after every algebraic-space base change.

source.place: Tag 05W8, forward implication; elementary common-field argument from spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 040X (lemma-universally-injective), (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Conversely, assume $g$ is unramified and universally injective. By [lem-sfb-space-unramified-radicial-representable], $g$ is representable by schemes. Fix any scheme $T\to Y$. The base change $g_T:X\times_YT\to T$ is consequently a scheme morphism. It is unramified by [lem-sfb-space-unramified-permanence]; applying the chart characterization [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts] to its identity scheme charts gives unramifiedness in the scheme sense. It is universally injective as a scheme morphism because every further scheme base change is among the algebraic-space base changes in the hypothesis. It is universally closed by the identical observation for closed maps and [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Thus [lem-sfb-universally-closed-unramified-radicial-criterion] makes $g_T$ a closed immersion. Since $T\to Y$ was arbitrary, this is precisely the stated scheme-test definition of a closed immersion of algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 05W8, last two sentences: representability from Tag 05W6, then scheme criterion Tag 04XV.
